context.problem_statement: Implement the Black-Scholes option pricing model to price European call and put options. For the given set of options (varying strike prices and maturities), compute: (1) call price and put price using the Black-Scholes formula, (2) all five Greeks: Delta, Gamma, Theta (per day), Vega (per 1% vol change), Rho (per 1% rate change), (3) verify put-call parity: C - P = S*exp(-q*T) - K*exp(-r*T). Spot price S=100, risk-free rate r=0.05, dividend yield q=0.02, implied volatility sigma=0.20.
context.expert_knowledge: Black-Scholes: d1 = (ln(S/K) + (r - q + sigma^2/2)*T) / (sigma*sqrt(T)), d2 = d1 - sigma*sqrt(T). Call = S*exp(-q*T)*N(d1) - K*exp(-r*T)*N(d2). Put = K*exp(-r*T)*N(-d2) - S*exp(-q*T)*N(-d1). Delta_call = exp(-q*T)*N(d1). Gamma = exp(-q*T)*n(d1)/(S*sigma*sqrt(T)). Use scipy.stats.norm for N() and n().
